observation_summary: The TypeUtils.getTypeArguments method fails to correctly resolve type arguments for classes that implement generic interfaces with specific type arguments when the class itself also declares type variables. This results in an empty or incomplete map of type arguments, causing assertion failures in tests.
hypothesis: The TypeUtils.getTypeArguments method fails to correctly traverse the class hierarchy when a class implements a generic interface with specific type arguments while also declaring its own type variables, leading to an incomplete mapping of type variables to their actual types.
prediction: The implementation of TypeUtils.getTypeArguments will show a logic error in how it handles the superclass/interface hierarchy traversal, specifically skipping or incorrectly processing classes that define their own type parameters.
experiment_rationale: The failure is clearly in the logic of the TypeUtils class, which is responsible for calculating type arguments. The bug report and test failures indicate that the algorithm for traversing the class hierarchy and mapping type variables is insufficient for cases where classes have their own type parameters. This is a procedural/algorithmic issue in the implementation of the reflection utility.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure in the algorithm used to resolve type arguments in the TypeUtils class. It is not a missing check (Checking), nor an incorrect initialization (Assignment/Initialization), nor a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object). It is a flaw in the procedural logic of the type resolution algorithm.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not a missing guard or validation, but a failure in the core logic of the type resolution algorithm.
The fix does not require a new class or a major design change, but rather a correction to the existing type resolution algorithm.
